flawed_step: The claimed reverse inclusion cl(A) ∩ cl(B) ⊆ cl(A ∩ B) fails for arbitrary subsets.
counterexample: Let X={0,1} with the indiscrete topology {∅,X}. Take A={0} and B={1}. Then A∩B=∅, so cl(A∩B)=∅. Since every nonempty subset of an indiscrete space has closure X, cl(A)=X and cl(B)=X, hence cl(A)∩cl(B)=X≠∅.
assessment_summary: The hypotheses hold, but the asserted equality fails in this two-point topological space.
